finding: Found relevant patterns: Python AES-256-GCM S3 encryption, Cognito UserPool+IdentityPool TOTP auth flow for temp credentials, client-side encryption best practices
KB has no direct nsync info. Found lesson: agent scoping - add Scope Boundaries + Available Tools sections to prompts for better behavior.
CLI has 9 commands: setup, get, add, rm, ls, pull, approve, rotate-key, import-pass. Trusted/untrusted device model with pending approval workflow.
Found key AWS docs: Cognito Identity Pool credentials, TOTP MFA config, S3 client-side encryption with AES-GCM, identity pool security best practices
CDK deploys: Cognito UserPool (TOTP required, 32-char min pwd, no recovery), IdentityPool, S3 bucket (versioned, SSE-S3, enforceSSL), IAM auth role. Stealth naming (config-sync, not password).

Full CLI structure mapped: 9 commands (setup/get/add/rm/ls/pull/approve/rotate-key/import-pass). Crypto: AES-256-GCM with 12-byte nonce. Auth: SRP+TOTP via pycognito. Store: single encrypted JSON blob in S3. Approval workflow: untrusted devices push to pending/ prefix, trusted device reviews.

Scripts: nsync-gui (curses TUI v1.4.0 with live search, auto-update, TOTP prompt), nsync-genpass (Bedrock Claude password gen), nsync-type.sh (fzf+keystroke), nsync_picker.py (tkinter GUI), pass-nsync.bash (pass wrapper), generate-setup.sh (device onboarding script gen)
Cognito auth flow for CLI: initiate-auth → get-id → get-credentials-for-identity gives temp AWS creds. With TOTP MFA, needs respond-to-auth-challenge step between initiate-auth and getting tokens.
Internal tools (InternalSearch, Atlas, SearchSoftwareRecommendations) all blocked by expired Midway credentials. Pivoting to AWS docs for security best practices and CDK patterns.

Security-critical paths: crypto.py (AES-256-GCM, 12-byte nonce, no AAD), auth.py (SRP+TOTP, refresh token caching, 1hr untrusted expiry), config.py (0o600 perms, 0o700 dir), store.py (path validation regex, version history). Tests: 545 lines covering crypto, store, config, sync, auth with mocks.
Lessons learned confirm: agent prompts should have Scope Boundaries section + Available Tools section. Critical Rules has highest ROI. Explicit tool lists > wildcard.

Cognito TOTP limitations: only HMAC-SHA1 supported, 5 failed MFA attempts triggers lockout, MFA code valid 3-15min. Identity pool credentials via STS. S3 Encryption Client v3 uses AES-256-GCM with key commitment.

AES-256-GCM best practices: random nonce per encryption, PBKDF2 600k iterations or Argon2id for key derivation, salt per encryption, authenticated associated data, no partial decryption on failure. Format: [version][salt][nonce][ciphertext+tag]

S3 conditional writes (If-Match ETag) can prevent concurrent overwrite conflicts - relevant for sync. Cognito token validity: ID/Access 5min-1day, Refresh 1hr-3650days. Identity pool credentials are temporary STS creds.
9 commands: setup, get [-c/-t], add [-f], rm, ls, pull, approve, rotate-key, import-pass. get -c copies to clipboard with 45s auto-clear. get -t types via AppleScript (macOS) or xdotool (Linux).

Cognito UserPool 'config-sync-users' (stealth name), TOTP MFA required, no SMS, no self-signup, 32-char min password, no account recovery, RETAIN. App client 'config-sync-cli': SRP auth, no secret, 1hr access/id tokens, 3650-day refresh token. S3 'config-sync-{account}': SSE-S3 (not KMS — intentional to avoid CloudTrail noise), versioned, RETAIN, enforceSSL, block all public. Identity Pool: no unauthenticated. IAM role 'config-sync-auth-role': full grantReadWrite on bucket (no path restriction).

Untrusted devices encrypt pending changes to S3 key pending/{timestamp}_{device_id}.enc using cloud_key. Trusted device runs 'nsync approve' to list/decrypt/apply or reject. TUI nsync-gui shows pending count and [A] to approve all. Pending objects are deleted after approve or reject.

5 scripts: nsync-gui (curses TUI with live search, pending approvals, auto-update from GitHub raw URL), nsync-genpass (Bedrock Claude Sonnet 4 password generation, hardcoded us-west-2), nsync-type.sh (fzf fuzzy picker + type-out), pass-nsync.bash (pass wrapper auto-sync), nsync_picker.py (tkinter GUI picker, Spotlight-launchable). Also generate-setup.sh in cli/.

crypto.py: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte random nonce prepended to ciphertext. auth.py: SRP+TOTP, refresh token cached, 1hr session enforcement for untrusted devices. config.py: 0o600 file, 0o700 dir. store.py: path validation regex + no '..' traversal, version history on overwrite. sync.py: all S3 ops use temporary STS credentials.

CONFIRMED BUG: nsync_picker.py line 'remote = sync.pull_store(creds, cfg)' then 'return remote["entries"]' — pull_store returns (dict, etag) tuple, not dict. 'if remote is None' check will never trigger. Accessing remote["entries"] raises TypeError. nsync_picker.py is completely broken.

nsync-gui fetches raw script from GitHub (REMOTE_URL) and overwrites itself without any signature verification. Supply chain attack vector: if GitHub account is compromised, all nsync-gui instances auto-update to malicious code.

IAM role config-sync-auth-role uses bucket.grantReadWrite(authRole) — grants s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket on entire bucket. Any authenticated Cognito user can read/write/delete any key including other users' pending/ objects. No per-user path restriction.

nsync-genpass hardcodes region_name='us-west-2' for Bedrock. Will fail if user's AWS account doesn't have Bedrock access in us-west-2 or if they prefer a different region. Should use cfg['region'] or a configurable default.

pass-nsync.bash calls 'nsync import-pass' after every pass insert/edit/generate/rm. import-pass re-imports the ENTIRE pass store each time (walks ~/.password-store, decrypts all .gpg files). Slow for large stores and makes unnecessary Cognito auth calls.

Agent prompt missing: (1) all 5 scripts and their purposes, (2) nsync-genpass Bedrock dependency, (3) stealth naming convention (config-sync-* not nsync-*), (4) version history feature in store, (5) 3650-day refresh token for trusted devices, (6) test suite (pytest in cli/tests/), (7) generate-setup.sh for device onboarding, (8) nsync_picker.py bug.

AWS docs confirm nsync follows best practices: SRP auth (recommended over plaintext), TOTP MFA, temp credentials via Identity Pool, S3 versioning, enforceSSL, BlockPublicAccess. CDK correctly sets both aud+amr trust policy conditions. One gap: IAM role grants full bucket ReadWrite — should scope to specific key prefixes (store.enc, pending/).

CDK UserPool with MFA: use mfa: cognito.Mfa.REQUIRED, mfaSecondFactor: {otp: true, sms: false}. Auth flow: initiate-auth → ChallengeName=SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA → respond-to-auth-challenge with TOTP code → get tokens → use IdToken with IdentityPool for temp AWS creds
